'''Ian Henry Grojnowski''' (born April 1966)<ref>{{cite web |url=https://find-and-update.company-information.service.gov.uk/officers/-yZFYex0W6-GbTCdL1PH1l4ysPU/appointments |title=Ian Grojnowski – Personal Appointments |publisher=Companies House |access-date=2026-08-24}}</ref> is a mathematician working at the [[Department of Pure Mathematics and Mathematical Statistics]] at the [[University of Cambridge]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.dpmms.cam.ac.uk/~groj/|title=Ian Grojnowski|website=www.dpmms.cam.ac.uk}}</ref>

==Awards and honours==
Grojnowski was the first recipient of the [[Fröhlich Prize]] of the [[London Mathematical Society]] in 2004 for his work in [[representation theory]] and [[algebraic geometry]]. The citation reads<ref>[http://www.lms.ac.uk/activities/prizes_com/citations04.html Grojnowski's citation from the London Mathematical Society] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20041231232542/http://www.lms.ac.uk/activities/prizes_com/citations04.html |date=2004-12-31 }}</ref>{{centered pull quote|Grojnowski's insights into geometric contexts for representation theory go back to his thesis with [[George Lusztig]] on character sheaves over homogeneous spaces.<ref>[http://www.dpmms.cam.ac.uk/~groj/thesis.ps Character sheaves on symmetric spaces] Ph.D. thesis by I. Grojnowski</ref> He has exploited these ideas to make breakthroughs in several completely unexpected areas, including representations of the [[affine Hecke algebra]]s at roots of 1 (generalising results of [[David Kazhdan|Kazhdan]] and Lusztig), the [[representation theory of the symmetric group]]s S<sub>''n''</sub> in [[characteristic (algebra)|characteristic ''p'']], the introduction (simultaneously with Nakajima) of vertex operators on the cohomology of the Hilbert schemes of finite subschemes of a complex [[algebraic surface]], and (in joint work with Fishel and Teleman) the proof of the strong Macdonald conjecture of Hanlon and Feigin for [[reductive Lie algebra|reductive]] [[Lie algebra]]s.}}
